_comment: Per-vendor wheel-tester defaults loaded by wheel_ffb.py. Edit values to retune; the daemon reads this on every run. `match` is a list of substrings checked against the evdev device name (case-insensitive) to pick the vendor preset. Booleans (e.g. "invert") — set true to enable. Numeric keys map to --flag=N when applied. Keys starting with '_' are ignored.

fanatec._comment: Fanatec CSL Elite WB via hid-fanatecff. hz=100 because hid-fanatecff's USB output saturates at the daemon default of 500. target-lpf-hz=8 smooths the incoming target stream; friction-deadband=0.020 prevents friction-comp limit-cycling near zero.

thrustmaster._comment: T300 + hid-tmff2. Belt-driven, ~0.08 stiction. Motor sign opposite encoder, hence invert. PID gains untested in the field — kept at the daemon defaults. target-lpf-hz and friction-deadband added by analogy with the Fanatec tuning (LPF kills slider-drag buzz; deadband prevents friction-comp limit-cycle near zero, scaled smaller than Fanatec's because friction-comp is smaller).

logitech._comment: G29/G920/G923/etc. Gear-driven. Native-evdev FF_CONSTANT comes out sign-flipped, hence invert. ki=3.0 (vs. ~0.1 elsewhere) winds the integrator quickly enough to clear gear stiction at the end of a move. kd=0.45 (half the original 0.85): the higher value chattered audibly during braking and on small target changes because gear backlash made d_current spike. friction-deadband=0.005 keeps steady-state offset under ~2° on a 900° G29. friction-comp reduced from 0.18 to 0.12 because the integrator now does most of the work — the leftover role of friction-comp is just to step through stiction at the deadband boundary, and a smaller value makes the on/off transition less audible.
